name: EXACT_CHANNEL_DECOMPOSITION_APPLICATION_CONTRACT

epistemic_firewall.structural_statement: The abstract two-block theorem is mathematically valid whenever its hypotheses hold.
epistemic_firewall.application_statement: Using it algorithmically on a new graph additionally requires a graph-only decomposition certificate and polynomially checkable application receipts.
epistemic_firewall.forbidden_inference: A valid theorem does not imply that discovering a suitable decomposition in an arbitrary input graph is polynomial.

required_fields: anchors c in L and f in R
port sets P_L subseteq L\{c}, P_R subseteq R\{f}
exact channel graph X=E(L,R) subseteq P_L x P_R
exact_interface_checks: Partition is total and pairwise disjoint.
Every L-R edge belongs to X.
Every X-edge has one endpoint in P_L and one in P_R.
No L-R edge exists outside X.
object_certificate.verification_complexity: Polynomial in |V|+|E| for a supplied decomposition certificate.

canonical_anchor_normal_form: Require exactly one common neighbor z.
Run exactly one implication-reachability instance for (z,c,f).
DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.unique_hub: z is the unique common neighbor when representable
DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.semantic_firewall: Applies to the pure exact-channel interface only; additional C11/source-role/semantic restrictions require separate analysis.
DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.orientation_policy: Choose one arbitrary orientation only to name L/R and construct D; the reverse orientation is the order-dual lattice and adds no representability/capacity information.
DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.representation_lattice: Upper-set lattice of the flexible SCC DAG.
DECOMPOSITION_DISCOVERABLE.uniqueness: Representation unique iff FLEXIBLE is empty.

procedure: Construct the bipartite channel graph X.
Compute k=nu(X) by exact bipartite maximum matching.
Preserve one maximum matching M of size k.
Preserve one minimum vertex cover U of X and verify |U|=k.
Use the abstract local theorem to conclude lambda_G(c,f)=k+1.
LOCAL_FORMULA_CERTIFIED.polynomiality: Bipartite matching and verification of M/U are polynomial.
LOCAL_FORMULA_CERTIFIED.exact_upper_cut: {z} union U is an explicit c-f separator of size k+1.

capacity_invariance.theorem: For any exact-channel representation of the same anchors (c,f), nu(X)=rho_G(c,f).
capacity_invariance.consequence: The first feasible representation for fixed anchors suffices to compute exact channel capacity.

LOCAL_TO_GLOBAL_TRANSFER_CERTIFIED.meaning: Whether the equality kappa(G)=lambda_G(c,f)=1+nu(X) has been certified.

structural_route.label: STRUCTURAL_AUTHORITY
mechanism: For every S with |S|<=k consider the component-refined quotient hat_B_S whose vertices are connected components of G[L-S], connected components of G[R-S], and surviving {z}.
If hat_B_S is connected for every such S, the abstract component-refined theorem gives kappa(G)>=k+1.
Together with the explicit cut {z} union U, conclude kappa(G)=lambda_G(c,f)=k+1.
structural_route.complexity_warning: Literal enumeration of all S with |S|<=k is not polynomial when k is unbounded; this route is not automatically an efficient recognition algorithm.

algorithmic_route.label: ALGORITHMIC_CERTIFICATION
procedure: Verify the supplied exact-channel decomposition graph-only.
Layer 1 immediately certifies lambda_G(c,f)=k+1 and gives kappa(G)<=k+1 via {z} union a minimum vertex cover.
Independently compute/certify the exact global vertex connectivity kappa(G) with a polynomial vertex-connectivity / minimum-vertex-cut algorithm.
If the certified value satisfies kappa(G)>=k+1, the previous upper bound forces kappa(G)=k+1=lambda_G(c,f).
algorithmic_route.equivalent_test: Because the abstract local theorem always gives kappa(G)<=k+1, transfer equality holds iff kappa(G)>=k+1, equivalently iff kappa(G)=k+1.
algorithmic_route.role: Polynomial recognition/certification of transfer once a decomposition certificate is available.
algorithmic_route.explanation_limit: This route certifies equality but does not by itself explain which structural mechanism makes every refined interface quotient robust.

equivalent_transfer_conditions: G-S is connected for every S subseteq V(G) with |S|<=k
hat_B_S is connected for every S with |S|<=k
exact_characterization.qualification: Use the standard non-small finite-graph convention in which vertex connectivity is the minimum size of a vertex set whose deletion disconnects the graph or leaves the applicable trivial case.

recognition_vs_certification.decomposition_discovery: Anchor-pair based and polynomial: a representable pair must be a nonedge with exactly one common neighbor z, followed by one fixed-triple reachability test.
recognition_vs_certification.local_formula_certification: Polynomial after graph-only discovery or a supplied valid decomposition.
recognition_vs_certification.local_to_global_equality_certification: Polynomial after discovery/supply of the decomposition, by bipartite matching plus exact vertex-connectivity computation.
recognition_vs_certification.structural_mechanism_classification: Separate explanatory task; examples include block robustness, component-refined external reconnection, hub redundancy, matching/cover geometry, or another proved mechanism.
recognition_vs_certification.canonical_solution_structure: For each feasible fixed triple, R_min and R_max are canonical extremal decompositions, and all feasible R-sides form a distributive lattice of implication-upsets between them.
recognition_vs_certification.negative_certificate: A forced-R to forced-L implication path is a compact proof-carrying NO-DECOMPOSITION certificate for a fixed triple.
recognition_vs_certification.capacity_selection: No optimization over this lattice is required because matching capacity is representation-invariant.
recognition_vs_certification.anchor_pair_firewall: Different anchor pairs of the same graph may have different rho_G(c,f). Any task optimizing capacity over anchors must still compare anchor pairs.
recognition_vs_certification.hub_selection: There is no hub-selection problem for fixed representable anchors: the hub is the unique common neighbor.
recognition_vs_certification.remaining_representation_freedom: Only the distributive lattice of implication-closed partitions for the unique hub remains.
recognition_vs_certification.anchor_orientation: Representability and capacity are properties of the unordered pair {c,f}. Reversing anchors complements feasible R-sides and dualizes the partition lattice.
recognition_vs_certification.forced_geometry: For one chosen orientation, forced-R, forced-L, and flexible vertices are exact; flexible SCCs are the atomic representation degrees of freedom.
recognition_vs_certification.uniqueness: Unique representation iff no flexible vertex exists, equivalently R_min=R_max.
recognition_vs_certification.representation_space: All remaining representation freedom is the upper-set lattice Up(H) of the flexible SCC-poset H.
recognition_vs_certification.compact_vs_enumerated: H is polynomially constructible, but |Up(H)| can be exponential. Do not enumerate or count all representations unless the task explicitly requires it.
recognition_vs_certification.counting_firewall: Generic finite-poset antichain counting is #P-complete, but exact-channel representation counting is NOT classified by this contract absent a realization/reduction theorem.
recognition_vs_certification.capacity_nonbranching: Capacity is representation-invariant, so canonical bottom R_min suffices; representation-space enumeration/counting is irrelevant to rho_G(c,f).

phase_A_exact_channel_decomposition_disc.question: Which authoritative C11 unordered anchor pairs satisfy the pure exact-channel normal form, and do extra C11 semantics distinguish an orientation?
graph_only_pipeline: compute F_R,F_L,F_star and flexible SCC-poset H
store H compactly instead of enumerating representations
use canonical bottom R_min=F_R for canonical ports/X and capacity
phase_A_exact_channel_decomposition_disc.orientation_firewall: If extra C11 roles make c and f semantically asymmetric, audit both semantic role assignments separately even though the pure graph object is reversal-dual.
phase_A_exact_channel_decomposition_disc.representation_space_firewall: Do not enumerate Up(H) during C11 surveys unless an experiment explicitly targets representation multiplicity. Capacity and canonical-channel diagnostics require only R_min.

phase_B_transfer_mechanism_classificatio.question: For discovered decompositions with certified equality kappa=lambda=1+nu(X), what structural mechanism explains the transfer?

discovery.negative: directed path r0 -> ... -> ell0, r0 in R0, ell0 in L0

capacity_invariant.representation_invariance: All other valid exact-channel representations with the same anchors have matching number k.

anchor_normal_form.fixed_triple_receipt: Reach_D(R0) intersect L0 empty, or a forced-R to forced-L path

normal_form.representation: R=FORCED_R union any upper set U of H
normal_form.reversal: opposite orientation uses complement R and the dual DAG

representation_space.counting_complexity_claim: must remain NOT_CLASSIFIED unless separately proved

easy_application_corollary.name: COMPACT_POSET_NORMAL_FORM_WITHOUT_REPRESENTATION_BRANCHING
easy_application_corollary.statement: For fixed pure exact-channel anchors, construct the polynomial-size normal form ({c,f},z,F_R,F_L,H). All valid representations are upper sets of H, but capacity is constant across them, so use the canonical bottom and never branch over the representation lattice for capacity or local-connectivity certification.
easy_application_corollary.caveat: The representation lattice itself may be exponentially large; explicit enumeration/counting is a separate problem.

next_action: No new gate from the poset normal form. For the next C11 survey, store only the compact forced/flexible/SCC-poset receipt and canonical bottom representation unless representation multiplicity is itself the preregistered target.
